title: A conservative point family detects acyclicity
statement: Let C be a category essentially small in the coefficient universe, J a Grothendieck topology, R a sheaf of commutative rings, p a point of Sh(C,J), and s a normalized ringed-site point [def-sfb-ringed-site-point], with stalk ring A and module functor S. For a set-indexed family (p_i,s_i) whose inverse images jointly reflect isomorphisms of set sheaves, a module complex K is acyclic if and only if every S_i(K) is acyclic. The family may be empty.

proof.text: Exact S_i preserve homology, hence preserve acyclicity.

The prescribed underlying-set isomorphisms transfer joint reflection of isomorphisms to module sheaves. If every stalk complex is acyclic, every map H^n(K) to zero is an isomorphism at each point. Joint reflection makes it an isomorphism, hence H^n(K) is zero. No point is selected; an empty conservative family is covered.

lean.statement:
theorem acyclic_iff
    {I : Type t} (p : I → GeometricMorphism (Type w) (Sheaf J (Type w)))
    (s : ∀ i : I, RingedSitePoint R (p i))
    (hp : JointlyReflectIsomorphisms (fun i : I ↦ (p i).inverse))
    (K : CochainComplex (ringedSiteModules.{w}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{w} RingCat.{w})).obj R)) ℤ) :
    K.Acyclic ↔ ∀ i : I,
      (((s i).modules.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj K).Acyclic
